new.label: Return to standard-care and exception-route assessment

old.title: Reassess the HCC treatment plan
old.when: An AFP requirement is unmet, tumor response is inadequate, or transplantation is currently unsuitable.
tasks: AFP level, AFP trajectory and radiographic viability answer different questions. Repeat an unexplained result, assess liver inflammation and obtain expert review of adequate multiphasic imaging; do not label AFP-only rise radiographic progression. No empiric LRT without a target. B1.1 proposals are OPEN, not automatic delisting rules.
Review AFP trend together with multiphase imaging, viable tumor, extrahepatic staging, liver function, performance status and prior toxicity.
Select a treatment below based on the findings and patient goals. An unmet AFP threshold alone does not show that every option is feasible.
After treatment, reassess response and liver function. Reconsider resection and transplant only when the full clinical and allocation criteria support them.

actions.label: Review systemic therapy or a clinical trial

old.title: Continue or change liver-directed treatment
old.when: There is treatable liver disease, and liver reserve and anatomy permit another local treatment.
tasks: Continue the current downstaging approach if it is producing useful tumor control and remains safe. If response is inadequate, review a different modality with interventional radiology and radiation oncology.
Options include ablation, arterial treatment such as TACE or Y90, and radiation such as SBRT. Select by viable tumor location, prior treatment, normal-liver exposure and liver function.

If no suitable viable target remains, clarify the AFP rise and staging before repeating liver-directed treatment. If local treatment is unsuitable or ineffective, review systemic therapy, a trial or best supportive care.
Recheck imaging and AFP after treatment, then reassess transplant and MELD-exception criteria.

actions.label: If local treatment is unsuitable: systemic options

old.title: Systemic therapy or a clinical trial
old.when: Liver-directed treatment is unsuitable or has not controlled the disease, or the disease extent favors systemic treatment.
tasks: AFP level, AFP trajectory and radiographic viability answer different questions. Repeat an unexplained result, assess liver inflammation and obtain expert review of adequate multiphasic imaging; do not label AFP-only rise radiographic progression. No empiric LRT without a target. B1.1 proposals are OPEN, not automatic delisting rules.

Medical oncology should choose the regimen using liver function, performance status, prior drugs, toxicity, bleeding risk and patient goals. Select subsequent-line therapy or a trial after progression when appropriate.

Most systemic-therapy evidence is in Child-Pugh A disease. Treatment in Child-Pugh B requires individual assessment; Child-Pugh C or progressive liver failure generally limits treatment to selected circumstances or trials.
If transplantation remains a possibility, discuss immune checkpoint inhibitors with transplant surgery, hepatology and pharmacy before treatment because later transplantation carries rejection risk.
For recurrence after liver transplantation, select systemic therapy jointly with the transplant team because checkpoint inhibitors can cause graft rejection.
After response, reconsider local treatment or surgery when feasible. If further tumor-directed treatment is unsuitable or declined, arrange best supportive care.

actions.label: Open the systemic therapy matrix
actions.detail: Compare treatment setting, biomarkers, pivotal trials and major precautions.

actions.label: Review immunotherapy and transplant timing
actions.detail: Previous checkpoint therapy requires assessment of immune toxicity and rejection risk; no washout interval guarantees safety.

old.title: Reassess liver resection
old.when: An HPB surgeon believes complete tumor removal may be feasible, including after a treatment response.
tasks: Reassess future liver remnant, liver function, portal hypertension and vascular/biliary anatomy. AFP failure alone is not an indication for surgery.
Offer resection only when the expected oncologic benefit and operative risk are acceptable. If resection is unsuitable, return to local or systemic treatment selection.
After resection, arrange HCC surveillance and reconsider treatment if recurrence develops.

old.title: Individual transplant and MELD-exception review
old.when: Standardized exception criteria are not met, but the transplant team considers an individually justified request.
tasks: Document pretreatment tumor burden, treatment response, AFP history, staging, liver function and expected transplant benefit. Review calculated MELD and donor options separately from an exception request.

For prior AFP >1,000, the standardized requirement remains a treatment response to <500 and continued AFP <500. NLRB guidance permits individual consideration in selected cases; approval is not assured.

For an AFP-only departure, arrange a high-risk HCC multidisciplinary review of AFP trend, treatment response, occult spread, liver reserve and expected benefit. The guidance generally views persistent AFP nonresponse unfavorably, but allows selected individual cases. The beyond-UNOS tumor-burden pilot has its own AFP <100 entry limit and is not an AFP-only protocol.
If the request is deferred or declined, continue an appropriate cancer-treatment or supportive-care plan. Do not leave the patient waiting without a care plan.

actions.label: Review the listing and exception evidence

old.title: Best supportive care
old.when: Further tumor-directed treatment is unsuitable, offers insufficient expected benefit, or is declined after discussion.
tasks: Arrange palliative care for symptom relief, psychosocial support and goals-of-care discussions.
Continue hepatology care for ascites, encephalopathy and other liver-disease complications; review symptom-directed radiation or procedures when expected benefit exceeds burden.
Agree follow-up and an urgent-contact plan; discuss hospice when appropriate. Palliative care can accompany cancer treatment.

actions.label: Reconsider cancer treatment if circumstances change

old.title: Continue planned follow-up
old.when: The treatment or transplant decision is complete and ongoing care has been agreed.
tasks: Confirm the responsible clinical team, surveillance schedule and plan for new symptoms or suspicious imaging.
After transplantation, review explant findings and continue transplant care. Adapt cancer surveillance to the diagnosis and recurrence risk; no single schedule fits every pathway.
If recurrence or a new safety problem is suspected, arrange prompt specialist review. After transplantation, treatment selection must account for graft function, immunosuppression and rejection risk.

The sarcoma and liver teams should compare resection, observation, local treatment and systemic treatment according to symptoms, distribution and disease behavior.
During observation or treatment, define which new symptoms or imaging changes require reassessment. Limited extrahepatic HEHE alone does not automatically exclude MELD-exception consideration.
Arrange best supportive care when further tumor-directed treatment is unsuitable or declined.

old.title: Best supportive care
old.when: Further tumor-directed treatment is unsuitable, offers insufficient expected benefit, or is declined after discussion.
tasks: Arrange palliative care for symptom relief, psychosocial support and goals-of-care discussions.
Review pain, effusions and other disease-related symptoms with the sarcoma team.
Agree follow-up and an urgent-contact plan; discuss hospice when appropriate. Palliative care can accompany cancer treatment.

old.title: Continue planned follow-up
old.when: The treatment or transplant decision is complete and ongoing care has been agreed.
tasks: Confirm the responsible clinical team, surveillance schedule and plan for new symptoms or suspicious imaging.
After transplantation, review explant findings and continue transplant care. Adapt cancer surveillance to the diagnosis and recurrence risk; no single schedule fits every pathway.
If recurrence or a new safety problem is suspected, arrange prompt specialist review. After transplantation, treatment selection must account for graft function, immunosuppression and rejection risk.

new.title: New or recurrent disease after transplantation
new.when: A liver transplant recipient has suspected or confirmed new or recurrent tumor.
tasks: Confirm the diagnosis and extent with the tumor and transplant teams, including the graft and extrahepatic sites.
Review graft function, immunosuppression, drug interactions and organ-specific treatment risks before choosing local or systemic therapy.

Review disease-specific treatment options with transplant specialists. An immune checkpoint inhibitor carries rejection and graft-loss risks after liver transplantation; for HCC, AASLD advises against routine post-transplant ICI.
Agree symptom management, a follow-up plan and a contact for worsening symptoms. This review does not authorize retransplantation.

actions.detail: Preserve graft and immunosuppression context.

old.title: Continue standard adenoma management
old.when: An HCA MELD-exception criterion is not met or transplantation is not justified.
tasks: Review hormone exposure, metabolic risk factors, subtype, size and growth with the benign liver tumor team.
Choose observation, resection or a suitable local treatment according to risk and feasibility. Set a surveillance and reassessment plan.
Treat active bleeding urgently. Investigate suspected malignant transformation through the appropriate cancer pathway.
For ongoing symptoms or liver disease, arrange hepatology and symptom-management follow-up even when transplantation is not indicated.

old.title: Treat unstable hemorrhage
old.when: There is hemodynamic instability from adenoma bleeding.
tasks: Arrange immediate resuscitation and urgent interventional-radiology and surgical assessment, including embolization where appropriate.
After stabilization, reassess residual viable adenoma, resection feasibility and the longer-term treatment plan.
